title: Open problem on lower bound for concentration interval
statement_text: For $p$ fixed, nothing is known from below concerning concentration: it has not even been shown that the chromatic number cannot be concentrated in an interval of constant length.
context_text: $\mathcal{G}(n,p)$ is the Erdős–Rényi random graph on $n$ vertices in which each pair is an edge independently with probability $p$; here $0<p<1$ is a fixed constant. Saying that $\chi(G)$ is concentrated in an interval of length $\ell(n)$ means that there is a function $h(n)$ such that, for $G\in\mathcal{G}(n,p)$, $|\chi(G)-h(n)|<\ell(n)$ with probability $1-o(1)$; $\omega(n)$ denotes any function tending to infinity. Shamir and Spencer proved concentration in an interval of length $\omega(n)\sqrt{n}$, and the paper gives a proof (of a result due to Alon) of concentration in an interval of length $\omega(n)\sqrt{n}/\log n$. For sparse random graphs much stronger results hold: Łuczak and Alon–Krivelevich obtained two-point concentration for $p<n^{-1/2-\epsilon}$. All these are upper bounds on the concentration width; for fixed $p$, the author notes that no lower bound is known, i.e. it has not been ruled out that $\chi(G(n,p))$ is concentrated on a bounded number of values. Bollobás is cited for further discussion of this question.
notes: Stated as a prose observation without a labelled theorem environment. The precise open question is whether one can rule out constant-length concentration of chi(G(n,p)) for fixed p.
paper_title: On the concentration of the chromatic number of random graphs
